clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old female with a history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes presented with right limb involuntary dance-like movements for 1 day. Initial lab tests showed severe hyperglycemia (random blood glucose 33.3 mmoL/L, HbA1c 17.85%) with negative urinary ketones. Head CT was negative for acute cerebral infarction, hemorrhage, or tumor. Brain MRI showed normal T1, T2, and DWI sequences, but low ADC signals and value in the left basal ganglia, contralateral to the chorea. The patient was diagnosed with non-ketosis hyperglycemic chorea. Treatment included intravenous insulin for hyperglycemia and oral haloperidol (HPD) for chorea. The dance-like movements gradually decreased after 3 days and disappeared after 4 days of HPD treatment.
